title: Comunicado 2025-11-20
summary: The MPC unanimously cut the repo rate 25bp to 6.75%, saying there was 'scope now to make the policy stance less restrictive' given an improved inflation outlook: recent prints undershot forecasts, the uptick to 3.6% is attributed to temporary non-core items (meat, vegetables, fuel), and a stronger rand and lower oil assumption trimmed the 2025-26 inflation forecasts, with risks balanced and expectations moving toward 3%. The Quarterly Projection Model still forecasts gradual rate cuts, but the rate path stays only a broad guide and decisions remain meeting-by-meeting; the two risk scenarios (a dollar rebound and a front-loaded electricity price correction) both imply slower easing. The statement also formalises the new 3% +/-1pp point target, stressing the Bank is not indifferent within the band and will do what is required to get back to 3%. Versus September, when the MPC held with a split committee (two members wanting a cut) and wanted to see how past easing and expectations played out, the committee has moved to a unanimous cut on a better inflation outlook, while the stricter target and tighter risk scenarios keep the further-easing signal gradual rather than committed.

key_quotes.quote: The decision was unanimous. Members agreed there was scope now to make the policy stance less restrictive, in the context of an improved inflation outlook.
key_quotes.context: Unanimous 25bp cut, after September's split hold

key_quotes.quote: The Quarterly Projection Model continues to forecast gradual rate cuts as inflation subsides. As before, this rate path remains a broad policy guide.
key_quotes.context: Further easing as a gradual, non-committal baseline; meeting-by-meeting

key_quotes.quote: We continue to see this pressure as temporary, with inflation heading lower again from the beginning of next year.
key_quotes.context: Recent uptick driven by non-core items, looked through

key_quotes.quote: The tolerance band, of 1 percentage point either side of 3%, does not mean we will be indifferent to inflation anywhere between 2% and 4%. We want to be at 3%.
key_quotes.context: New point target adds a hawkish anchor to the easing message
